events.summary:
H1 is strongly grounded at the symptom layer and is almost certainly the right *mechanism*: onset is pinned to 12:12Z (metrics + first ERROR log 12:12:31Z), the single change event in the window is dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0, 12:10Z, 12 min before onset, adds MarginCheckValidator, removes legacy OrderRules.validateMargin()), and all 426 errors are the same local NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.java:88 with marginProfile null on orderType=FNO, with flat latency/CPU/pool ruling out resource exhaustion (H4 rejected on solid evidence). However two things stop this from being accept-ready: (1) the causal hop "removing legacy validateMargin() is what makes marginProfile null" is unverified — the code provenance of marginProfile (local vs remote lookup) has never been established, so H2's origin (a dependency path returning null) is not contradicted, only unqueried; (2) the onset-vs-deploy alignment rests on a single 12:10Z deploy whose F&O path may have gone live at 12:12Z for reasons never checked (rollout staging / traffic-by-orderType). Neither gap is fatal but both are obtainable and could change the ranking, so the 0.82 confidence is not defensible yet.

Note on H2/H3 severity: their contradictions are largely sound (portfolio-service flat is the only verified dependency; H3's rejection cites the NPE signature, which is a real argument against a datastore-IO origin). But H2's own contradiction claim — "no dependency telemetry showing a coincident fault exists only because it was not queried" — is correctly self-flagged; redis-cache error_rate and per-dependency onset were never read. H2 is not required to be false for H1's *mechanism* to be true, but it does change **which component is the fix target** (rollback order-service vs fix a dependency/account-data path), so it is a major, not minor, issue.

On calibration: confidence_cap 0.68 reflects a well-established symptom, a well-established timeline, and a well-established candidate change — but an unverified provenance hop for the null.

Bounded requests below (2, not 4): both are cheap, both target the one decisive unknown, and both are answerable by tools that have worked this round.

Also state, from code/schema, whether marginProfile is constructed locally in order-service or fetched from a remote dependency (and if remote, which one). Settles the unverified causal hop and distinguishes H1 (origin in order-service code) from H2 (origin in a data-providing dependency).

Query redis-cache error_rate and latency (plus the metric lists for redis-cache, ledger-db and kafka so actual metric names are known) for 11:00-14:00Z, and report whether any changes at or before 12:12Z. Also fill the T3 gap by checking the remaining unverified dependencies (ledger-db, kafka, other DBs) for error_rate/latency degradation at or before 12:12Z.

events.summary: H1 is now adequately supported and the alternatives are contradicted by evidence rather than merely unqueried. Symptom layer is solid: onset pinned at 12:12Z by per-minute metrics (0.20%→17.97%) and the first ERROR log at 12:12:31Z; all 426 errors are the same local signature, NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.validate(MarginCheckValidator.java:88) with marginProfile null on orderType=FNO; latency_p99, cpu_pct, memory_pct and db_pool_in_use are flat across 11:00-14:00Z, so failures are fast rejections not resource-bound (H4 correctly rejected). Change layer is now fully inventoried: dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0, 12:10:00Z, 'add margin check for F&O orders' / 'remove legacy OrderRules.validateMargin()') is the ONLY deployment across all services in the window (F3, F27) and the ONLY margin-related change; config inventory is complete (F5, F28, cfg-2101 unrelated), so the "need a full-window config list" concern is resolved — no gap remains that could hide a relevant change in the reported window. H2's decisive hop has now been chased and failed: order-service's full downstream closure contains no margin/account lookup service (F25), ledger-db is a telemetry-bearing leaf with no downstream edges (F26), and the only topology-consistent shared-cache mechanism (redis transitive to pricing-engine/market-data-service, HIST-107) has benign-latency symptoms, not fast FNO-only 500s (F29). H2's own data-side mechanism is directly measured flat at the onset: redis hit_ratio 95.94%@12:10 → 95.16%@12:15, evictions and cpu flat (F21, F22), ledger-db slow_queries and replication_lag flat (F23). H3's remaining leg (kafka) is unmeasured, but kafka has no path to produce a typed marginProfile null at code line 88, so its absence does not gate H1. The unread code diff is a legitimate residual gap but it is a secondary detail of an otherwise established origin: the provenance of marginProfile is now constrained by topology (no remote provider exists), so the fix target — roll back dep-5101 — is not genuinely in dispute. Remaining uncertainty (whether removal of populate versus read-before-populate, kafka/metrics coverage, whether the change was staged to 12:12) is reason for a confidence cap and stated assumptions, not for another round. Spending the remaining ~20 calls would not move the ranking and costs minutes during a SEV-1.

H1 is strongly grounded at the symptom layer and is almost certainly the right *mechanism*: onset is pinned to 12:12Z (metrics + first ERROR log 12:12:31Z), the single change event in the window is dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0, 12:10Z, 12 min before onset, adds MarginCheckValidator, removes legacy OrderRules.validateMargin()), and all 426 errors are the same local NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.java:88 with marginProfile null on orderType=FNO, with flat latency/CPU/pool ruling out resource exhaustion (H4 rejected on solid evidence). However two things stop this from being accept-ready: (1) the causal hop "removing legacy validateMargin() is what makes marginProfile null" is unverified — the code provenance of marginProfile (local vs remote lookup) has never been established, so H2's origin (a dependency path returning null) is not contradicted, only unqueried; (2) the onset-vs-deploy alignment rests on a single 12:10Z deploy whose F&O path may have gone live at 12:12Z for reasons never checked (rollout staging / traffic-by-orderType). Neither gap is fatal but both are obtainable and could change the ranking, so the 0.82 confidence is not defensible yet.

Note on H2/H3 severity: their contradictions are largely sound (portfolio-service flat is the only verified dependency; H3's rejection cites the NPE signature, which is a real argument against a datastore-IO origin). But H2's own contradiction claim — "no dependency telemetry showing a coincident fault exists only because it was not queried" — is correctly self-flagged; redis-cache error_rate and per-dependency onset were never read. H2 is not required to be false for H1's *mechanism* to be true, but it does change **which component is the fix target** (rollback order-service vs fix a dependency/account-data path), so it is a major, not minor, issue.

On calibration: confidence_cap 0.68 reflects a well-established symptom, a well-established timeline, and a well-established candidate change — but an unverified provenance hop for the null.

Bounded requests below (2, not 4): both are cheap, both target the one decisive unknown, and both are answerable by tools that have worked this round.

challenges.issue: The key hop — that marginProfile was populated by the removed OrderRules.validateMargin() (or an equivalent step) and that its removal/reordering is what produces null — is an ASSUMPTION with zero supporting evidence. The code provenance of marginProfile (locally constructed vs remotely fetched) has never been established. Without it, H1 and H2 share the identical downstream chain (null -> line 88 -> NPE -> 500 on FNO); only the origin differs, and the origin is what determines the fix.

Temporal tightness is asserted from a single 12:10Z-12:12Z alignment. F4 calls the 12-minute gap 'precedes onset', but nothing verifies the F&O validation path went live at 12:12Z rather than v2.14.0 being only partially active (staged rollout / flag flip) or F&O volume simply starting then. A ~12-min deploy-to-symptom lag is compatible with both H1 and a data-side origin that only materialized when writes landed.

H2 is not contradicted on its merits — the only sound contradiction is portfolio-service being flat, but portfolio-service may not be the margin data source at all (no margin-service/account-service exists per F11). redis-cache error_rate was never read and no per-dependency onset comparison was run, so the dependency-side null source is untested rather than excluded. H2 names a DIFFERENT origin and a DIFFERENT fix than H1, so it cannot be dismissed at 0.22 on absent data.

The 'derivatives-only' scope claim rests on error-signature text (orderType=FNO) rather than an endpoint-level error split, and the log result was truncated (40 of 191 returned, window only 12:05-13:00Z). F18's inference that ~18-19% error share equals the F&O traffic share is an assumption, not measured. If non-FNO orders also 500, the 'specific FNO null path' framing weakens.

H3's rejection is well-argued (NPE signature, flat pool/latency, fast rejections) but its exclusion of shared ledger-db/redis-cache/kafka rests partly on data never pulled: DB metric names for ledger-db/kafka were never retrieved and the shared-datastore precedent search failed with a 503. Not blocking, since the NPE signature is strong positive evidence against an IO/timeout origin.

Change inventory completeness is only 2/3 proven: the deployment query returned no pre-10:00Z baseline, so an earlier dependency deploy still settling cannot be excluded; the config-change full-window query timed out and was split (absence in the split boundary unproven). This weakens the 'single candidate change event' claim that H1's causal chain's first hop depends on.

evidence_requests.question: Diff the order-service validation path between v2.13.x (pre-dep-5101) and v2.14.0: specifically, did the removed legacy OrderRules.validateMargin() populate or trigger population of marginProfile, and does MarginCheckValidator.java:88 read marginProfile before any population step? Also state, from the code/schema, whether marginProfile is constructed locally in order-service or fetched from a remote dependency (and if remote, which one).
evidence_requests.rationale: This single question settles the one unverified hop in H1's causal chain and decides between H1 (origin in order-service code) and H2 (origin in a data-providing dependency) — the two hypotheses name different fixes. It is the cheapest decisive evidence and no tool query so far has addressed provenance.

evidence_requests.question: Query redis-cache error_rate and latency (and the metric list for redis-cache, ledger-db and kafka so their actual metric names are known) for 11:00-14:00Z, and report whether any of them changes at or before 12:12Z. If redis-cache exposes a cache-miss or null-response metric, include it.
evidence_requests.rationale: H2's only remaining live mechanism is a shared datastore/cache returning null for F&O accounts at ~12:12Z. This has never been queried (explicit GAP: 'Could not query redis-cache error_rate'). A flat redis-cache would convert H2 from 'untested' to 'contradicted'; a coincident degradation would promote it.

critiques.summary: H1 is now adequately supported and the alternatives are contradicted by evidence rather than merely unqueried. Symptom layer is solid: onset pinned at 12:12Z by per-minute metrics (0.20%→17.97%) and the first ERROR log at 12:12:31Z; all 426 errors are the same local signature, NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.validate(MarginCheckValidator.java:88) with marginProfile null on orderType=FNO; latency_p99, cpu_pct, memory_pct and db_pool_in_use are flat across 11:00-14:00Z, so failures are fast rejections not resource-bound (H4 correctly rejected). Change layer is now fully inventoried: dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0, 12:10:00Z, 'add margin check for F&O orders' / 'remove legacy OrderRules.validateMargin()') is the ONLY deployment across all services in the window (F3, F27) and the ONLY margin-related change; config inventory is complete (F5, F28, cfg-2101 unrelated), so the "need a full-window config list" concern is resolved — no gap remains that could hide a relevant change in the reported window. H2's decisive hop has now been chased and failed: order-service's full downstream closure contains no margin/account lookup service (F25), ledger-db is a telemetry-bearing leaf with no downstream edges (F26), and the only topology-consistent shared-cache mechanism (redis transitive to pricing-engine/market-data-service, HIST-107) has benign-latency symptoms, not fast FNO-only 500s (F29). H2's own data-side mechanism is directly measured flat at the onset: redis hit_ratio 95.94%@12:10 → 95.16%@12:15, evictions and cpu flat (F21, F22), ledger-db slow_queries and replication_lag flat (F23). H3's remaining leg (kafka) is unmeasured, but kafka has no path to produce a typed marginProfile null at code line 88, so its absence does not gate H1. The unread code diff is a legitimate residual gap but it is a secondary detail of an otherwise established origin: the provenance of marginProfile is now constrained by topology (no remote provider exists), so the fix target — roll back dep-5101 — is not genuinely in dispute. Remaining uncertainty (whether removal of populate versus read-before-populate, kafka/metrics coverage, whether the change was staged to 12:12) is reason for a confidence cap and stated assumptions, not for another round. Spending the remaining ~20 calls would not move the ranking and costs minutes during a SEV-1.

challenges.issue: The specific internal hop — that marginProfile was populated by the removed OrderRules.validateMargin(), or that line 88 reads it before population — is still unverified because no tool exposes the v2.13.x→v2.14.0 diff (T4 answered 'cannot obtain'). Two mechanisms (removed populate step vs read-before-populate) are conflated; both are consistent with the observed null, so it does not change the fix target, but the stated causal chain is stronger than the evidence.

Assumption that no earlier (<10:00Z) deploy on a dependency is responsible rests on an incomplete inventory: no pre-10:00Z deployment baseline was pulled (GAPS), and dep-5088 (portfolio-service v4.2.1, 09:36Z, grpc bump) exists 2h34m before onset. That timing gap plus the flat portfolio-service error_rate make it very unlikely, but it is an assumption rather than a verified absence.

The 'F&O failure is near-total' claim equates the ~18-19% error share with the F&O traffic share; there is no per-endpoint or per-orderType error-rate split (no such metric exists) and the ERROR log result was truncated (40 of 191), so the derivatives-only conclusion rests on signature text alone. This bounds the claimed blast radius, not the origin.

The 12:10Z deploy → 12:12Z symptom lag is unexplained (staging / first F&O traffic at 12:12Z never tested), and the change was never rolled back by 13:59Z, so removal of the deploy has not been confirmed to clear the symptom. This is corroborative evidence that was not collected, not a contradiction.

Not refuted at the code/schema level (no schema access for marginProfile), only by topology: no margin/account service in the closure (F25), ledger-db a leaf (F26), and no coincident redis/ledger degradation (F21-F23). Aggregate hit_ratio could in principle conceal a narrow key-level null, so the contradiction is strong but indirect.

kafka metrics were never obtained (all error_rate attempts failed/timed out; metric list never retrieved), so the kafka leg is unmeasured rather than refuted. However kafka cannot emit a typed marginProfile null into order-service code, so it does not gate H1's origin.
